title: Introduction to GitHub Actions knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Introduction to GitHub Actions?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.

questions.answer_key: GitHub Actions runs workflows defined in repository YAML files when configured events occur; jobs run on runners and are made of ordered steps.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of introduction to github actions: GitHub Actions runs workflows defined in repository YAML files when configured events occur; jobs run on runners and are made of ordered steps. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to introduction to github actions?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: GitHub Actions runs workflows defined in repository YAML files when configured events occur; jobs run on runners and are made of ordered steps. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
